chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid narrated to us, he said: Al-Hasan ibn Mutayyal the flour merchant narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to us, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Umar al-Karabisi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The best of your youths is the one who resembles your old ones, and the worst of your old ones is the one who resembles your youths.
ai.seo_question: What is the ideal behavior for youth and elders according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this maxim from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to highlight the ideal of *tashabbuh* (imitation) as a mechanism for moral continuity between generations. It serves as a critique of social inversion, urging youth to emulate the wisdom and composure of elders while warning the elderly against losing their dignity by adopting the frivolity of the young. This reciprocal relationship underscores the Shia emphasis on preserving communal honor through age-appropriate conduct.
